title: Heywood councillor apologises for Christmas lights switch-on after stray firework and 'mediocre' display
excerpt: North Heywood councillor Bev Place has apologised after families said a stray firework went into the crowd at Heywood's Christmas lights switch-on, calling the display mediocre.
body:
North Heywood councillor Bev Place has apologised for Heywood's Christmas lights switch-on, after families said a stray firework went into the crowd on Saturday 14 November.

Parents said they had to run with young children when the firework came towards them. As far as we know, nobody was hurt.

Witnesses believe the display was stopped suddenly because of the stray firework.

One parent said: "We figured it stopped because of the one that went into the crowd (we saw it as it was maybe a meter or two away from my 3 year old). I really think we need an explanation for what happened or some kind of statement and apology. Absolutely beyond disgusted."

Another said: "We were nearly hit by a firework, had to run away with a young child. Think that's why they stopped so abruptly!"

In a public statement on Sunday 15 November, Cllr Place said: "I've read all of the disappointed posts about last nights Xmas Lights Switch-on and I wanted to apologise and explain what happened."

She said: "What followed, in terms of the display was mediocre, in my opinion. What I don't know yet is whether that was what we paid for, or if it was halted due to the stray firework."

Cllr Place said Heywood Business Group, which organised the event independently for 17 years, had decided it was time to pass it on. Heywood Township funded the switch-on as usual, but with no organiser the job fell to the Rochdale Development Agency, "and with that, much more red tape than has previously been required."

She said The Queen Anne, which had hosted the fireworks in previous years, was not deemed a safe enough location, and the necessary insurance could not be obtained.

"With 1 week to go, we had no safe location for the fireworks and I was beyond stressed," Cllr Place said.

Heywood Civic then agreed to let a specialist fireworks company, which carried its own insurance, use its roof. Cllr Place said the council accepted that insurance as sufficient.

She said: "No, the fireworks weren't as good but we did what we could with our £10k budget."

Cllr Place said Environmental Management brought bin lorries to block off the road, saving £6,000 that would otherwise have been spent on hard stops.

She compared Heywood with Middleton, where she said the fireworks cost £6,000, are delivered by a private company, and are sponsored by the owners of Middleton Arndale and let off from its roof.

She also pointed to the rest of the day: traders in the market, a Santa's grotto, free face painting, a brass band, the fairground, stalls on Peine Square, two shows at Heywood Civic, Heywood Rotary's Santa's sleigh and performances by local children at St Luke's. The Mayor and Mayoress, two stars from Heywood Panto and the MP led the countdown.

Heywood and Middleton North MP Elsie Blundell, who attended with her child, posted afterwards: "Heywood looks fabulous this evening! Thank you to all of the organisers of today's events and the Christmas lights switch on." Her post did not mention the stray firework.

Heywood Christmas Lights Switch On, the group behind the event, posted a statement after the display. It did not address the stray firework.

It said: "The Christmas Light Switch On has been organised by the Heywood Business Group for many years along with the 1940s Day, Roch Valley Radio agreed to take on both events however, for the Christmas Lights this year the event had already started being organised by the RDA and council to ensure the event was to go ahead, this meant that it had to meet the councils insurance requirements. We are taking the feedback on how Roch Valley Radio can manage it like the business group at next years event."

The RDA is the Rochdale Development Agency, the council's economic development arm.

In the summer, Heywood Township's delegated sub-committee was asked to put £10,000 towards this year's switch-on, with fireworks and a day of family entertainment. The Rochdale Development Agency was expected to cover the rest of the estimated £12,650 cost.

Cllr Place said she has "lots of questions" that she will be asking on Monday 16 November.

Rochdale Daily has asked the organisers about the stray firework and what precautions will be taken next year.

Source: eyewitness accounts, a public statement by Cllr Bev Place, a statement from Heywood Christmas Lights Switch On and a public post by Elsie Blundell MP. Photograph: Elsie Blundell MP / Facebook.
